# Blender Project — Instructions

Highland cinematic film: [30-second graded owner film, stills and editable scene](deliverables/highland-cinema/README.md) · [shot list and rebuild](projects/highland-drone/CINEMA.md).

Highland architectural walkthrough: [upgraded full film, phone preview and Blender scene](deliverables/highland-archviz/README.md).

Highland installation: [90-second installation animation and downloads](deliverables/highland-installation/README.md) · [source project and editable-model setup](projects/highland-installation/README.md).

Purpose: build dimensionally accurate, realistic 3D models of Michael's restoration and defect-repair projects (occupied multifamily) from construction drawings, details, specs, and site photos, using Blender driven by Python. Accuracy first, realism second. A model is finished only when every dimension traces to a source or is labeled as assumed, the automated checks pass, and the renders have been looked at.

Operator procedure with exact commands: **RUNBOOK.md**.

Saved-model rendering: [GitHub Actions workflow, shot catalog and operating guide](render/README.md).

## Pipeline (always in this order)

1. **Intake.** Inventory every source: sheet number, detail number, revision/date, scale, photo IDs. Read drawings at full resolution (rasterize PDFs with `pdftoppm -r 200+`; crop into details). Note scale bars and "NTS" details.
2. **Takeoff.** Extract every dimension, member size, spacing, elevation, and count into the model spec. Use actual lumber sizes (2x10 = 1½ × 9¼), not nominal. Never scale an NTS detail. Never infer a dimension from a partial drawing and call it documented.
3. **Model spec** (`specs/<project>-<area>.yaml`). The spec is the single source of truth; geometry is never hand-edited in Blender without the spec changing too. Every element carries:
   - `status: confirmed` — dimension shown on a document (`source` required)
   - `status: provisional` — derived: scaled from a drawing with a scale bar, or measured from a photo against a known reference (`source` required; note the reference and expected tolerance)
   - `status: assumed` — not in any document (`basis` required, e.g. "code-minimum", "typical", "massing only")
   - Document-driven `checks`: counts, overall extents, clear gaps, spacing, elevations — each with its `source`.
4. **Build.** `python tools/build.py specs/<name>.yaml [--realistic]` (bpy, headless). One collection per trade; trades stay separate. Inches in the spec; Blender stores meters, displays imperial.
5. **Verify.** The builder fails (exit 1) on: missing source/basis, count or extent mismatch, gap mismatch, or a blank render. Then look at the review renders myself — plan, front, side, iso — colored by provenance (green confirmed, yellow provisional, orange assumed). Where a drawing elevation exists, compare the ortho render against it at the same scale. "Checks passed" and "looked right" are both required; report which were done.
6. **Realism pass** (only after geometry is verified). PBR materials by real product where known; realistic lighting via Cycles. Realism never changes geometry.
7. **Quantities.** Every house build writes `<name>_takeoff.xlsx` (tools/qto.py): openings schedule, siding + gable panel net of openings by elevation, casing and corner-board LF, roof area by pitch, squares (waste is a yellow input), ridge/hip/valley/eave/rake LF, and an Elements sheet of stable IDs for trackers. Measured values are blue inputs with method + status; everything derived is a live formula. Reconcile against any documented quantity (Cottage A: plan roof area 3,935.7 vs 3,935 sf on AH202).
8. **Deliver.** `.blend` (editable), `.glb` (phone/web viewing, carries element metadata), review renders, `report.md`. List every assumed element in the handoff.

## Plan-set method (proven on QP Cottage A, 2026-09-27)

- **Calibrate every sheet from its own dimension strings** before measuring anything: find the tick marks of a long dimension and compute pt/ft (AH201: 39'-0" ticks 702 pt apart = 18.0 pt/ft = true 1/4"). Never trust the title-block scale alone.
- **Rasterize at an exact scale** (2 px/in plans, 1–2 px/in elevations). Walls drawn as hollow outlines are found as thin enclosed white cores (half-width 2.5–7.5 px); window glazing splits the band into strips under 2.3 px half-width.
- **Every extracted opening must appear on an elevation** or it is rejected (tubs, showers, garage-door lines and revision clouds all produce false openings). Record rejected candidates in the spec.
- **Revision clouds and tags break linework** — look for missing wall where a cloud crosses, trace it manually, and add it as an `extra_walls` entry with its reason.
- **Mirror-image units:** extract the cleaner half and mirror, but first measure the match (Cottage A: 94% of walls within 1½").
- **Roofs:** union of convex hip/gable pieces taken from the eave outline on the roof plan; verify predicted ridge/hip positions against the drawn ones and ridge heights against elevations.
- **Walls are built boolean-free** (rectangle decomposition, openings cut by box splitting). Roof unions use Blender's **Manifold** boolean solver — the Exact solver fails on the coplanar faces that roofs inevitably have.
- **Overlay check:** `tools/overlay.py` renders the model orthographically at the drawing's scale and overlays it on the elevation; report the edge-agreement % and look at the image.

## Model types

- **detail** — one construction section (rake, eave, balcony edge, window head) as callout-sized components swept along a short path; 1/16" intent. `tools/detail.py`.
- **house** — plan-extracted shell (walls, openings, roof) + quantity takeoff. `tools/house.py`, `tools/qto.py`.
- **room** — interior shell + furniture + lighting from a photo or sketch (`specs/room-*.yaml`, `tools/room.py`). Photo-only, so nothing can be `confirmed`: every group is `provisional` (visible, sized from a reference) or `assumed`. Checks are internal consistency (body corners match the spec, clearances, footprints don't overlap), not accuracy to the real room. `tools/build.py` hands room specs to `room.py` (checks + review renders only, so CI needs no workflow change). Run `python tools/room.py specs/room-living-kitchen.yaml [--only review_iso,photomatch_night] [--no-render]`; the full render set is ~25 min on 4 CPU cores.
- **element / building** — not built yet: parametric components (balcony, stair) and multi-level buildings with repeated units.
All types share: provenance on every element, failing checks, CI rebuild.

## Accuracy rules

- Never present an assumed or provisional element as documented. Review renders always show provenance colors; realistic renders shared outside the team must carry a note if any assumed elements are visible.
- Photos: state the reference object used for scale (brick course, CMU, door, siding exposure, known member size), the camera angle limits, and the resulting tolerance. Photo-only geometry is at best `provisional`.
- Conflicts between sources (drawing vs. photo vs. spec): model per the governing document, flag the conflict in the report — don't average or silently pick.
- Existing-conditions models (defect repair) and proposed-repair models are separate scenes or separate specs. Don't merge them.
- Models are illustrative/coordination tools, not contract documents. Any render used in a scope, PCO, or resident notice gets that label.

## Occupied-building use cases

Resident notices (what's happening at their unit), access and sequencing diagrams, protection/staging/egress layouts, and PCO backup showing concealed conditions. For these, include the relevant occupied-building elements (egress paths, protection, staging area, work zone) as their own collection, marked by source like everything else.

## Environment facts (verified 2026-09-27)

- `pip install bpy==5.0.1` works on Python 3.11 in Claude's Linux workspace; build + checks for a small spec run in seconds.
- Headless has no GPU: **Workbench and EEVEE render blank frames** — use Cycles on CPU only. Cameras need explicit rotation (track-to constraints are not evaluated before headless renders).
- Exports confirmed working: .blend, .glb, .obj, .stl, .fbx, .usdz. SVG import add-on present. IFC (Bonsai) not installed — unverified.
- Cycles realistic render: ~2 min for 4 review views + 1 realistic view at 1600×1200 on 2 CPU cores. EEVEE took 45 s for a trivial scene and still returned blank.

## CI

Workflow: `.github/workflows/build-models.yaml` (edit it in the GitHub web UI — Claude's token can't write workflow files).

GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/build-models.yml`) rebuilds changed specs on every PR and push to main, fails the PR if any check fails, writes each report to the job summary, and uploads `build/` as an artifact. Claude does the takeoff and spec edits; CI makes the geometry reproducible and blocks unsourced or inconsistent changes.

## Working style

Ask once, batched, only for what can't be read from the documents (e.g. a missing detail, which revision governs). Otherwise take the next step and mark assumptions. Don't claim a model is accurate beyond what its sources support.

# Organize & optimize the blender-models workflow

## Context
The repo grew from one spec-driven pipeline (`specs/` + `tools/`) into a lot of Highland deliverables, each with its own scripts, dependencies and workflows. The result:
- **Docs drift:** `INSTRUCTIONS.md` is an outdated copy of `README.md` (it lacks the room model type, the deliverable links and the CI note). There's no `CLAUDE.md`, so every agent session re-learns the rules.
- **Layout:** `projects/highland-drone/` (~30 files) holds four separate products: the drone tour, the archviz stills, the native Blender film and the cinema film. Deliverables are duplicated: `highland-blender` and `highland-archviz` share the same mp4, gif and poster, and `highland-installation` has copies of files from `projects/`.
- **Weight:** the git pack is 821 MB. About 50 mp4/blend/gif/html/pdf files are committed as plain blobs. LFS is used in only 5 folders, and the `git lfs` client isn't installed locally. `projects/highland-installation` already has a working pattern for large files: `release-assets.json` (a sha256 manifest of GitHub Release assets) plus `restore_assets.py`.
- **CI/env:** the `build-models.yaml` path filter points at `build-models.yml`, so edits to the workflow don't trigger it. Five workflows each run their own `pip install bpy==5.0.1 …`. There are 7 requirements and package files.

Decisions: cover all four areas, and **no history rewrite**. Existing blobs stay in the pack; we only stop adding new ones.

Constraint: Claude's token can't push changes under `.github/workflows/`. Workflow edits go into one patch file that the user applies through the GitHub web UI, or pushes with their own credentials.

Work goes in as **4 small PRs, in order**, so each one is easy to review and revert.

---

## PR 1 — Docs & agent guidance (no behavior change)
1. **Delete `INSTRUCTIONS.md`.** `README.md` is the up-to-date superset. Change any links to INSTRUCTIONS.md to point at README.md (`grep -rn INSTRUCTIONS`).
2. **Make `README.md` short:** purpose, a repo map (table: area → folder → entry command → doc), and a deliverables index (one row per `deliverables/<name>` with its source project and link). Move the long pipeline, plan-set method, accuracy rules and environment facts into **`docs/METHOD.md`**, word for word. `RUNBOOK.md` stays as the operator procedure; rename it to `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.
3. **Add `CLAUDE.md`** (short, under ~80 lines):
   - Non-negotiables: provenance statuses, never present assumed as confirmed, spec is the source of truth, Cycles CPU only when headless, actual lumber sizes.
   - Commands: build a spec, run tests, render a scene, restore assets.
   - Where things go: specs, tools, projects, deliverables, releases.
   - Large-file rule from PR 3: no new binary over 1 MB in plain git.
   - Workflow-file limitation.
   - Local machine: Iris Xe, no UE/GPU. Heavy renders go to Actions or RunPod.
4. **Add a standard `projects/<name>/README.md` header** to each project: *Purpose · Inputs · Commands (prepare → build → render → package) · Outputs → deliverables/… · Release tag.* Fill it in for highland-water, -repipe, -exterior, -installation and -drone, using what the existing READMEs already say.

## PR 2 — Repo layout
1. **Split `projects/highland-drone/`** by product, using `git mv` (keeps file history):
   - `projects/highland-drone/`: drone tour (`flight.spec.json`, `render.cjs`, `template.html`, `app.js`, `prepare.py`, `package.py`, `finish.py`, `audio.py`, `build.sh`, `osm-buildings-source.json`, `source-review/`, `assets/`)
   - `projects/highland-archviz/`: `archviz.py`, `review_archviz.py`, `package_archviz_film.py`

# Organize & optimize the blender-models workflow (uv, multi-project)

## Context
The repo grew from one spec-driven pipeline (`specs/` + `tools/`) into a lot of one-off work for 200 W. Highland, while other jobs sit loose in `specs/` (QP Cottage A, a field parapet, a living/kitchen room). Current problems:
- **Not reusable across jobs.** Highland has ~6 sibling folders (`projects/highland-*`, `deliverables/highland-*`). Other sites have no home folder: their specs, takeoff and sources are scattered. Starting a new construction project means copying things by hand.
- **Docs drift:** `INSTRUCTIONS.md` is an outdated copy of `README.md`, and there's no `CLAUDE.md`.
- **`projects/highland-drone/`** mixes four products: drone tour, archviz stills, native Blender film and cinema film. Some deliverables are byte-identical: `highland-blender` and `highland-archviz` share the same mp4, gif and poster.
- **Weight:** the pack is 821 MB, with ~50 binaries committed as plain blobs. LFS is used in only 5 folders and isn't installed locally. `projects/highland-installation/{release-assets.json,restore_assets.py}` already does checksum-verified GitHub Release assets.
- **Environment:** 7 requirements and package files, `pip install bpy==5.0.1` repeated across 5 workflows, and no lockfile. Local Python is 3.14, but bpy 5.0.1 needs 3.11. uv 0.12 is installed.
- **CI bug:** the `build-models.yaml` path filter points at `build-models.yml`.

Decisions: **uv is the only Python toolchain. Organize by site, so any construction project of any type fits the same shape. No history rewrite.** Claude's token can't push `.github/workflows/`, so workflow changes ship as a patch for the user to apply.

---

## Target shape
```
pyproject.toml  uv.lock  .python-version (3.11)
src/bmodels/                 # today's tools/*.py, as an installable package
  cli.py                     # `bm` entry point
  build.py house.py detail.py room.py qto.py overlay.py calibrate.py extract_plan.py
  anim/ (anim_common, animate_house, animate_sequence)  render/ (render_plan, render_scene, render_assets)
  assets.py  checks.py  project.py (loads project.yaml / product.yaml)
templates/project/           # skeleton `bm new` copies
projects/<site>/
  project.yaml               # name, address, client, building type, units, release tag, default tolerances
  sources/manifest.json      # sha256 + sheet/photo inventory (binary sources gitignored → Releases)
  specs/*.yaml               # spec-driven models: detail | house | room | element | building
  takeoff/                   # qto outputs worth versioning
  products/<product>/        # bespoke pipelines (film, viewer, walkthrough, report)
    product.yaml             # kind, steps {prepare, build, render, package: command}, outputs, release asset manifest
    README.md
  deliverables/<product>/    # small previews + README; large files linked from Releases
docs/ METHOD.md RUNBOOK.md   CLAUDE.md   README.md
```
Mapping of what exists today:
- `projects/highland/`: products `water`, `repipe`, `exterior`, `installation`, `drone`, `archviz`, `blender-film`, `cinema`, `owner-tour`. The `highland-drone` split is described in PR 3.
- `projects/qp-cottage-a/`: `specs/qp-cottage-a.yaml`, `qp-rake-ah700-12.yaml`, `takeoff/qp-cottage-a.json`.
- `projects/field-parapet/`: existing and proposed specs.
- `projects/room-living-kitchen/`: the room spec.
- `templates/project/specs/_sample-bay.yaml`: the sample spec becomes the template's example.

Generic tooling only takes a site name. Products keep their own scripts, and `product.yaml` declares how to run them, so `bm` can drive any product without knowing its internals.

---

## PR 1 — uv foundation (no file moves yet)
1. **`pyproject.toml`**: `requires-python = "==3.11.*"`, `.python-version` = 3.11 (uv downloads it, so there's no clash with the system's 3.14). Dependencies:
   - Core deps: `bpy==5.0.1`, `pyyaml`, `openpyxl`, `pillow`, `numpy`.
   - `[dependency-groups]`:
     - `pdf` (pymupdf, reportlab)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Render and finish the Highland cinematic film on one NVIDIA GPU (e.g. RTX 4090).
#
#   bash projects/highland-drone/runpod_render.sh setup          # Python 3.11, bpy 5.0.1, assets, scene checks
#   bash projects/highland-drone/runpod_render.sh bench uhd       # one frame per shot, projected hours
#   bash projects/highland-drone/runpod_render.sh render uhd 2    # all frames, 2 processes sharing the GPU
#   bash projects/highland-drone/runpod_render.sh finish uhd      # grade, titles, score, encode 4K + 1080p, checks
#   bash projects/highland-drone/runpod_render.sh all uhd 2       # everything above in order
#
# Profiles: uhd   = 3840 x 1608, 96 samples: 4K master plus a 1080p cut (default);
#           final = native 1920 x 804, 128 samples: 1080p master only.
# Rendering resumes where it stopped; existing frames are skipped.
# DEVICE=CUDA uses CUDA kernels if OptiX is unavailable on the driver.
set -euo pipefail
STAGE=${1:-all}; PROFILE=${2:-uhd}; WORKERS=${3:-2}; DEVICE=${DEVICE:-OPTIX}
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd); cd "$ROOT"
LOG=build/highland-cinema/logs; mkdir -p "$LOG"
BPY=.venv-bpy/bin/python; FIN=.venv-finish/bin/python
MASTER=1080; [ "$PROFILE" = uhd ] && MASTER=2160

setup() {
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
  if [ ! -f "$LOG/.apt-done" ]; then
    apt-get update -q
    apt-get install -y -q ffmpeg git-lfs libx11-6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxi6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libice6 libgl1 libegl1
    git lfs install --skip-smudge
    touch "$LOG/.apt-done"
  fi
  command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
  # bpy 5.0.1 needs exactly Python 3.11; uv downloads it if the image lacks it.
  [ -x "$BPY" ] || uv venv -p 3.11 .venv-bpy
  [ -x "$FIN" ] || uv venv -p 3.11 .venv-finish
  # Always reconcile dependencies: a venv left by an older setup may lack newer ones.
  uv pip install -p "$BPY" bpy==5.0.1 pillow
  uv pip install -p "$FIN" -r projects/highland-drone/requirements-cinema.txt
  # Poly Haven CC0 textures and models, verified against the committed lock (about 190 MB).
  "$BPY" projects/highland-drone/cinema_assets.py
  # cinema.py rebuilds the base walkthrough unless its own validation report is clean and
  # current, then prepares the cinema scene and checks every film camera; CPU, a few minutes.
  # A failed camera check must stop the pipeline before any GPU time is spent.
  if ! "$BPY" projects/highland-drone/cinema.py --validate --only 0 > "$LOG/setup-cinema.log" 2>&1; then
    tail -20 "$LOG/setup-cinema.log"; echo "Cinema scene preparation or camera validation failed"; exit 1
  fi
  grep -E "validated" "$LOG/setup-cinema.log"
}

bench() {
  "$BPY" projects/highland-drone/cinema.py --reuse --device "$DEVICE" --profile "$PROFILE" --bench 2>&1 \
    | grep -E "Cycles devices|BENCH|SHOT|Error|refusing" | tee "$LOG/bench-$PROFILE.log"
}

render() {
  # Bind the frame folder to the prepared scene once; stale frames are moved aside.
  if ! "$BPY" projects/highland-drone/cinema.py --reuse --profile "$PROFILE" --claim-frames > "$LOG/claim-$PROFILE.log" 2>&1; then
    tail -5 "$LOG/claim-$PROFILE.log"; exit 1
  fi
  grep -E "Moved" "$LOG/claim-$PROFILE.log" || true
  pids=()
  for k in $(seq 0 $((WORKERS-1))); do
    "$BPY" projects/highland-drone/cinema.py --reuse --device "$DEVICE" --profile "$PROFILE" --worker "$k/$WORKERS" \
      > "$LOG/render-$PROFILE-$k.log" 2>&1 &
    pids+=($!)
  done
  echo "Rendering with $WORKERS workers; follow progress with: tail -f $LOG/render-$PROFILE-*.log | grep SHOT"
  status=0; for p in "${pids[@]}"; do wait "$p" || status=1; done
  total=$(find "build/highland-cinema/frames/$PROFILE" -name '[0-9]*.png' ! -name '*.tmp.png' | wc -l)
  echo "Frames on disk: $total / 630"
  [ "$status" = 0 ] && [ "$total" = 630 ]
}

finish() {
  "$FIN" projects/highland-drone/cinema_finish.py --profile "$PROFILE" --master "$MASTER"
  ls -la deliverables/highland-cinema
}

case "$STAGE" in
  setup) setup ;;
  bench) bench ;;
  render) render ;;

name: Render saved Blender scenes

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "render/**"
      - "tools/render_*.py"
      - "tests/test_render_workflow.py"
      - "deliverables/**"
      - "projects/**"
      - ".github/workflows/render-scenes.yaml"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "render/**"
      - "tools/render_*.py"
      - "tests/test_render_workflow.py"
      - "deliverables/**"
      - "projects/**"
      - ".github/workflows/render-scenes.yaml"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      shot:
        description: "Shot ID from render/scenes.json, or all"
        type: string
        default: all
      profile:
        description: "Render quality"
        type: choice
        options: [preview, final]
      OUTPUT: build/scene-renders/${{ matrix.shot }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          lfs: true
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: render/requirements.txt
      - name: Install headless Blender runtime
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -q
          sudo apt-get install -y -q libx11-6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxi6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libice6 libgl1
          python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check -r render/requirements.txt
      - name: Check render validation rules
        run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_render_workflow.py
      - name: Render selected scene and camera
        env:
          SHOT: ${{ matrix.shot }}
          PROFILE: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.profile }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$OUTPUT"
          set -o pipefail
          python -u tools/render_scene.py --shot "$SHOT" --profile "$PROFILE" \
            --device CPU --output "$OUTPUT" 2>&1 | tee "$OUTPUT/render.log"

**What PR 1 changes:**
- **Python setup:** `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.python-version` (3.11) replace the six `requirements*.txt` files. Optional extras are uv dependency groups: `pdf`, `vision`, `audio` and `dev`.
- **One environment:** bpy 5.0.1 needs numpy older than 2, and opencv 5 needs numpy 2 or newer. - **Docs:** all venv and pip instructions now use `uv sync` / `uv run python`, including the generated READMEs in the installation project.

CI passed on PR #24's first run: the build job ran on bpy 5.0.1 installed through uv. Every spec rebuilt with all its checks passing, and the bpy render job passed too.

The one red check, "Entire Gates", is the external approval check, not a repo workflow. It failed for two reasons:
- **No approval:** nobody has approved the PR yet. That one is for you.
- **"16 commits behind":** my local `main` was stale. `origin/main` had picked up a new site, Meydenbauer Building B (PRs #18–#23), which I hadn't seen. I rebased onto it. The merge was clean.

Meydenbauer brought its own pip and venv setup, so I moved it onto uv as well:
- `shapely` is now a core dependency.
- Both of its RunPod scripts now install with `uv sync --frozen` and run with `uv run --no-sync`.
- Its README and REALISM commands use `uv run python`.

I force-pushed the rebased branch and added a note about this to the PR description. CI is running again.

Meydenbauer isn't checked by CI under uv. `build-models` only builds files in `specs/`, and Meydenbauer has its own `build.py` that nothing runs automatically. Its `build.py --no-render` takes about 3 seconds, so it's a good early user of the generic `bm build` / `bm check` in PR 2. It also shows why the site-generic layout matters: a second building arrived with its own copy of the RunPod scripts, venv setup and paths.

I'll report when the re-run finishes. The approval is the only part I can't clear myself.

def load_shots(catalog=CATALOG, root=ROOT):
    data = json.loads(Path(catalog).read_text())
    if data.get("schema_version") != 1:
        raise ValueError("Expected catalog schema_version 1")
    shots = data.get("shots")
    if not isinstance(shots, list) or not 1 <= len(shots) <= 128:
        raise ValueError("Catalog must contain between 1 and 128 shots")
    seen = set()
    for shot in shots:

        shot_id = shot.get("id", "")
        if not isinstance(shot_id, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}", shot_id):
            raise ValueError("Shot IDs must use lowercase letters, digits, underscores or hyphens")
        if shot_id == "all":

        'Highland-repipe-90s.blend',

        record = records[name]
        if path.stat().st_size != record['bytes'] or digest(path) != record['sha256']:
            raise ValueError(f'Release checksum mismatch: {name}')
        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:

                info = archive.getinfo(member)
                target = ROOT / relative
                if target.exists():
                    with archive.open(info) as source:
                        expected = hashlib.file_digest(source, 'sha256').hexdigest()
                    if digest(target) != expected:
                        raise FileExistsError(f'Preserving a modified local asset: {target}')

    restored = 0
    for name, members in archives.items():
        with zipfile.ZipFile(args.asset_directory / name) as archive:
            for member, relative in members.items():
                target = ROOT / relative
                if target.exists():
                    continue
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                temporary = target.with_name(target.name + '.part')
                try:
                    with archive.open(member) as source, temporary.open('xb') as output:
                        shutil.copyfileobj(source, output)
                    temporary.replace(target)
                finally:

                restored += 1
    print(f'Release archives verified; restored {restored} assets. Existing matching assets preserved.')

"""`bm` — one entry point for every construction project in the repo.

    bm list [--markdown]                       sites, specs and products
    bm new <site> [--type element|detail]      start a site from templates/project
    bm build [target ...] [--changed BASE]     build + verify specs (path, site, or site/spec)
    bm run <site>/<product> <step> [args]      run a product step from its product.yaml
    bm assets pull|verify|push <manifest> ...  release assets with checksums
    bm check [--staged | --base REF]           specs, metadata, large files, links, tests
    bm <tool> [args]                           calibrate, extract, overlay, detail-overlay, render,
                                               render-plan, animate-house, animate-sequence,
                                               room, skp, usdz

Run through uv: `uv run bm …`. Nothing here imports bpy; Blender work runs in a subprocess.
"""
import argparse
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from bmodels import assets, checks, project, spec
from bmodels.paths import BUILD, PROJECTS, ROOT, TEMPLATES

TOOLS = {  # bm <name> -> python -m bmodels.<module>
    "calibrate": "calibrate",
    "extract": "extract_plan",
    "overlay": "overlay",
    "detail-overlay": "detail_overlay",
    "render": "render_scene",
    "render-plan": "render_plan",
    "animate-house": "animate_house",
    "animate-sequence": "animate_sequence",
    "room": "room",
    "skp": "skp_code",
    "usdz": "export_usdz",
}
# Anything under these paths can change every build, so a change rebuilds every spec.
REBUILD_ALL = ("src/", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock", ".github/", "takeoff/")


def rel(p):
    return Path(p).resolve().relative_to(ROOT)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- list / new
def cmd_list(a):
    rows = []
    for s in project.sites():
        rows.append((s.name, s.meta.get("name", ""), [sp.stem for sp in s.specs], [p.name for p in s.products]))
    legacy = project.legacy_specs()
    if a.markdown:
        print("| Site | Name | Specs | Products |\n|---|---|---|---|")
        for site, name, sps, prods in rows:
            print(f"| [{site}](projects/{site}/) | {name} | {', '.join(sps) or '—'} | {', '.join(prods) or '—'} |")
        if legacy:
            print(f"| specs/ (unassigned) | | {', '.join(sp.stem for sp in legacy)} | |")
        return 0
    for site, name, sps, prods in rows:
        print(f"{site}  {name}")
        for sp in sps:
            print(f"  spec     {site}/{sp}  [{spec.kind(spec.load(PROJECTS / site / 'specs' / f'{sp}.yaml'))}]")
        for p in prods:
            print(f"  product  {site}/{p}")
    if legacy:
        print("specs/ (not yet assigned to a site)")
        for sp in legacy:
            print(f"  spec     {rel(sp)}  [{spec.kind(spec.load(sp))}]")
    return 0


def cmd_new(a):
    dest = PROJECTS / a.site
    if dest.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"{rel(dest)} already exists")
    tpl = TEMPLATES / "project"
    fill = {"{{site}}": a.site, "{{name}}": a.name or a.site}

    def render(src, out):
        text = src.read_text()
        for k, v in fill.items():
            text = text.replace(k, v)
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(text)

    for src in tpl.rglob("*"):
        if src.is_dir() or src.parent.name == "specs":
            continue
        out = dest / src.relative_to(tpl)
        if src.name == ".gitkeep":
            out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            out.touch()
        else:
            render(src, out)
    render(tpl / "specs" / f"{a.type}.yaml", dest / "specs" / f"{a.site}-{a.type}.yaml")
    print(f"Created {rel(dest)}/ — fill project.yaml and sources/manifest.json, then edit "
          f"specs/{a.site}-{a.type}.yaml and run: uv run bm build {a.site}")
    return 0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- build
def changed_specs(base):
    try:
        files = checks._git("diff", "--name-only", f"{base}...HEAD")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        files = checks._git("diff", "--name-only", base, "HEAD")
    files = [f for f in files if f]
    if any(f.startswith(REBUILD_ALL) for f in files):
        return project.all_specs()
    picked = set()
    for s in project.sites():
        d = str(rel(s.dir)) + "/"
        # specs read takeoff/sources data from anywhere in the site except products and deliverables
        if any(f.startswith(d) and not f.startswith((d + "products/", d + "deliverables/")) for f in files):
            picked.update(s.specs)
    picked.update(ROOT / f for f in files if f.startswith("specs/") and f.endswith(".yaml") and (ROOT / f).exists())
    return sorted(picked)


def cmd_build(a):
    specs = changed_specs(a.changed) if a.changed else project.resolve_specs(a.targets)
    if not specs:
        print("No specs to build.")
        return 0
    flags = (["--realistic"] if a.realistic else []) + (["--no-render"] if a.no_render else [])
    summary = os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY")
    failed = []
    for sp in specs:
        out = project.build_dir(sp)
        gh = bool(os.environ.get("GITHUB_ACTIONS"))
        print(f"::group::{rel(sp)}" if gh else f"== {rel(sp)} -> {rel(out)}/{sp.stem}/", flush=True)
        code = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "bmodels.build", str(sp), "--out", str(out), *flags]).returncode
        if gh:
            print("::endgroup::")
        if code:
            failed.append(rel(sp))
        report = out / sp.stem / "report.md"
        if summary and report.exists():
            with open(summary, "a") as f:
                f.write(report.read_text() + "\n")
    print(f"\n{len(specs) - len(failed)}/{len(specs)} specs passed" + (f"; failed: {', '.join(map(str, failed))}" if failed else ""))
    return 1 if failed else 0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- run / tools
def cmd_run(a):
    p = project.product(a.product)
    steps = p.meta.get("steps") or {}
    if a.step not in steps:
        raise SystemExit(f"{p.ref} has no step '{a.step}'. Steps: {', '.join(steps)}")
    cmds = steps[a.step] if isinstance(steps[a.step], list) else [steps[a.step]]
    env = {**os.environ, "BM_SITE": p.site.name, "BM_PRODUCT": p.name, "BM_PRODUCT_DIR": str(p.dir),
           "BM_BUILD": str(p.build), "BM_DELIVERABLES": str(p.deliverables)}
    for i, cmd in enumerate(cmds):
        if a.args and i == len(cmds) - 1:
            cmd += " " + " ".join(map(_quote, a.args))
        print(f"$ {cmd}", flush=True)
        code = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", cmd], cwd=ROOT, env=env).returncode
        if code:
            return code
    return 0


def _quote(s):
    import shlex
    return shlex.quote(s)


def run_tool(module, args):
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", f"bmodels.{module}", *args]).returncode


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- assets / check
def cmd_assets(a):
    if a.action == "verify":
        return 0 if assets.verify(a.manifest, a.from_dirs) else 1
    if a.action == "pull":
        assets.pull(a.manifest, a.names or None, a.from_dirs)
        return 0
    if not a.names:
        raise SystemExit("bm assets push <manifest> <file> [file ...]")
    assets.push(a.manifest, a.names)
    return 0


def cmd_check(a):
    sections = [("specs", checks.specs()), ("site/product metadata", checks.metadata())]
    files = checks.changed_files(a.staged, a.base)
    if a.staged or a.base:
        sections.append(("large files", checks.large_files(files)))
    if not a.staged:
        sections.append(("markdown links", checks.links()))
    failed = False
    for name, errors in sections:
        print(f"{'FAIL' if errors else 'ok  '}  {name}" + "".join(f"\n      {e}" for e in errors))
        failed |= bool(errors)
    if not a.no_tests and not a.staged:
        failed |= subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q"], cwd=ROOT).returncode not in (0, 5)
    return 1 if failed else 0


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- main
def parser():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="bm", description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("list", help="sites, specs and products")
    p.add_argument("--markdown", action="store_true")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_list)

    p = sub.add_parser("new", help="start a site from templates/project")
    p.add_argument("site", help="folder name, lowercase-hyphenated (e.g. qp-cottage-a)")
    p.add_argument("--name", help="display name (default: the site folder)")
    p.add_argument("--type", choices=["element", "detail"], default="element", help="starter spec")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_new)

    p = sub.add_parser("build", help="build and verify specs")
    p.add_argument("targets", nargs="*", help="spec path, site, or site/spec (default: all)")
    p.add_argument("--changed", metavar="BASE", help="only specs affected by changes since BASE")
    p.add_argument("--realistic", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--no-render", action="store_true")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_build)

    p = sub.add_parser("run", help="run a product step from its product.yaml")
    p.add_argument("product", help="site/product")
    p.add_argument("step")
    p.add_argument("args", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER, help="appended to the step's last command")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_run)

    p = sub.add_parser("assets", help="release assets with checksums")
    p.add_argument("action", choices=["pull", "verify", "push"])
    p.add_argument("manifest", type=Path)
    p.add_argument("names", nargs="*", help="pull: asset names (default all); push: files to upload")
    p.add_argument("--from", dest="from_dirs", action="append", default=[], metavar="DIR",
                   help="also look for verified copies here (e.g. manually downloaded ZIPs)")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_assets)

    p = sub.add_parser("check", help="specs, metadata, large files, links, tests")
    g = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    g.add_argument("--staged", action="store_true", help="pre-commit: staged files only, fast checks")
    g.add_argument("--base", metavar="REF", help="CI: also check files added since REF")
    p.add_argument("--no-tests", action="store_true")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_check)

    for name, module in TOOLS.items():
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=f"python -m bmodels.{module}", add_help=False)
        p.add_argument("args", nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
        p.set_defaults(fn=lambda a, m=module: run_tool(m, a.args))
    return ap


def main(argv=None):
    a = parser().parse_args(argv)
    return a.fn(a) or 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""bm CLI, spec validation and release-asset restore (no bpy, no network)."""
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from bmodels import assets, cli, project, spec
from bmodels.paths import ROOT, TEMPLATES


class SpecTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_repo_and_template_specs_validate(self):
        paths = project.all_specs() + sorted((TEMPLATES / "project/specs").glob("*.yaml"))
        self.assertTrue(paths)
        for path in paths:
            with self.subTest(spec=path.name):
                self.assertEqual(spec.check(spec.load(path)), [])

    def test_unsourced_element_fails(self):
        s = {"sources": [], "elements": [{"id": "a", "size": [1, 1, 1], "at": [0, 0, 0], "trade": "t", "status": "confirmed"}]}
        self.assertTrue(any("source" in e for e in spec.check(s)))

    def test_assumed_needs_basis(self):
        s = {"sources": [], "elements": [{"id": "a", "size": [1, 1, 1], "at": [0, 0, 0], "trade": "t", "status": "assumed"}]}
        self.assertTrue(any("basis" in e for e in spec.check(s)))


class AssetTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.downloads = self.tmp / "downloads"
        self.downloads.mkdir()
        (self.downloads / "film.mp4").write_bytes(b"film")
        with zipfile.ZipFile(self.downloads / "model.zip", "w") as z:
            z.writestr("pkg/model.blend", b"blend")
        records = []
        for name in ("film.mp4", "model.zip"):
            p = self.downloads / name
            records.append({"name": name, "bytes": p.stat().st_size, "sha256": assets.digest(p)})
        records[0]["dest"] = "out/film.mp4"
        records[1]["extract"] = {"pkg/model.blend": "models/model.blend"}
        self.manifest = self.tmp / "release-assets.json"
        self.manifest.write_text(json.dumps({"tag": "t", "assets": records}))

    def test_pull_restores_dest_and_extract(self):
        assets.pull(self.manifest, extra_dirs=[self.downloads])
        self.assertEqual((self.tmp / "out/film.mp4").read_bytes(), b"film")
        self.assertEqual((self.tmp / "models/model.blend").read_bytes(), b"blend")
        self.assertTrue(assets.verify(self.manifest, [self.downloads]))

    def test_pull_preserves_modified_target_and_writes_nothing(self):
        (self.tmp / "models").mkdir()
        (self.tmp / "models/model.blend").write_bytes(b"edited")
        with self.assertRaises(FileExistsError):
            assets.pull(self.manifest, extra_dirs=[self.downloads])
        self.assertFalse((self.tmp / "out/film.mp4").exists())  # all-or-nothing

    def test_corrupt_download_is_not_used(self):
        (self.downloads / "film.mp4").write_bytes(b"flim")
        self.assertFalse(assets.verify(self.manifest, [self.downloads]))


class NewSiteTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_new_site_from_template_validates(self):
        tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        old = cli.PROJECTS
        cli.PROJECTS = tmp
        try:
            for kind in ("element", "detail"):
                self.assertEqual(cli.main(["new", f"demo-{kind}", "--type", kind, "--name", "Demo"]), 0)
                site = tmp / f"demo-{kind}"
                self.assertIn('name: "Demo"', (site / "project.yaml").read_text())
                self.assertTrue((site / "products/.gitkeep").exists())
                s = spec.load(site / "specs" / f"demo-{kind}-{kind}.yaml")
                self.assertEqual(spec.kind(s), kind)
                self.assertEqual(spec.check(s), [])
                self.assertNotIn("{{", (site / "README.md").read_text())
        finally:
            cli.PROJECTS = old

    def test_paths_point_at_repo(self):
        self.assertTrue((ROOT / "pyproject.toml").exists())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""External render assets referenced by a scene, excluding saved UI paths."""
from pathlib import Path


def scene_asset_paths(bpy, scene):
    # user_map maps an ID to its users. Invert it to walk from this scene to
    # objects, materials, node groups, images, worlds and other referenced IDs.
    dependencies = {}
    for dependency, users in bpy.data.user_map().items():
        for user in users:
            dependencies.setdefault(user, set()).add(dependency)
    pending = [scene]
    visited = set()
    paths = set()
    file_types = (bpy.types.Image, bpy.types.VectorFont, bpy.types.Sound,
                  bpy.types.MovieClip, bpy.types.Volume, bpy.types.CacheFile,
                  bpy.types.Library)
    while pending:
        item = pending.pop()
        if item in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(item)
        pending.extend(dependencies.get(item, ()))
        library = item.library
        if library:
            pending.append(library)
        if isinstance(item, bpy.types.Library) and item.parent:
            pending.append(item.parent)
        if not isinstance(item, file_types):
            continue
        path = item.filepath
        if not path or path == "<builtin>":
            continue
        if getattr(item, "packed_file", None) or getattr(item, "packed_files", None):
            continue
        if isinstance(item, bpy.types.Image) and item.source in ("GENERATED", "VIEWER"):
            continue
        # Indirect libraries and linked textures resolve relative to the
        # library that owns them, rather than the current working directory.
        owner = item.parent if isinstance(item, bpy.types.Library) else library
        paths.add(bpy.path.abspath(path, library=owner))
    return sorted(paths)


def validate_scene_assets(bpy, scene):
    paths = scene_asset_paths(bpy, scene)
    missing = [path for path in paths if not Path(path).is_file()]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing external scene assets (pack or restore them first): {missing}")
    return paths

"""Open committed .blend files and fail if any external file they reference is missing.

    uv run bm audit-blends [file.blend ...]     # default: every tracked .blend (LFS pointers are skipped)

Moving folders silently breaks relative paths saved inside .blend files (textures, linked libraries,
sounds); this catches it. Runs in bpy, so `bm` calls it in a subprocess.
"""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import bpy

from bmodels.paths import ROOT
from bmodels.render_assets import scene_asset_paths

LFS_POINTER = b"version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1"


def tracked_blends():
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "*.blend"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return [ROOT / f for f in out.split()]


def audit(path):
    if path.read_bytes()[:len(LFS_POINTER)] == LFS_POINTER:
        return {"file": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), "skipped": "LFS pointer (run with LFS checked out)"}
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=str(path))
    paths = sorted({p for scene in bpy.data.scenes for p in scene_asset_paths(bpy, scene)})
    missing = [p for p in paths if not Path(p).is_file()]
    return {"file": str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), "external": len(paths), "missing": missing}


def main():
    files = [Path(f).resolve() for f in sys.argv[1:]] or tracked_blends()
    results = [audit(f) for f in files]
    for r in results:
        state = "skip" if "skipped" in r else ("FAIL" if r["missing"] else "ok  ")
        print(f"{state}  {r['file']}  " + (r.get("skipped") or f"{r['external']} external files"), flush=True)
        for m in r.get("missing", []):
            print(f"        missing: {m}")
    print(json.dumps({"audited": sum("skipped" not in r for r in results),
                      "skipped": sum("skipped" in r for r in results),
                      "failed": sum(bool(r.get("missing")) for r in results)}))
    sys.exit(1 if any(r.get("missing") for r in results) else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Move folders with git mv and keep every reference working.

usage: python migrate.py MAPPING.json [--dry-run]
MAPPING: {"old/prefix": "new/prefix", ...} (repo-relative, longest prefix wins)

1. Resolve every relative markdown link in tracked .md files against the OLD layout.
2. git mv each mapped path.
3. Rewrite each markdown link relative to its file's NEW location.
4. Rewrite repo-root path strings (e.g. 'projects/x/y.py') in text files, never inside ../ links.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip())
MAPPING = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())
DRY = "--dry-run" in sys.argv
TEXT = (".md", ".py", ".sh", ".cjs", ".js", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".toml", ".html", ".txt", ".csv")
LINK = re.compile(r'(\]\(<?)([^)\s>]+)(>?(?:\s+"[^"]*")?\))')
SKIP = ("uv.lock", "package-lock.json")


def git(*a):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def remap(rel):
    """New repo-relative path for an old one (unchanged if unmapped)."""
    for old in sorted(MAPPING, key=len, reverse=True):
        if rel == old or rel.startswith(old + "/"):
            return MAPPING[old] + rel[len(old):]
    return rel


files = [f for f in git("ls-files").split("\n") if f and not f.endswith(SKIP)]
text_files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(TEXT) and (ROOT / f).is_file()]

# 1. collect markdown links against the old layout
links = {}  # old md path -> list of (span text, old target rel or None)
for f in text_files:
    if not f.endswith(".md"):
        continue
    src = (ROOT / f).read_text(errors="ignore")
    for m in LINK.finditer(src):
        url = m.group(2)
        if re.match(r"[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:", url) or url.startswith(("#", "/")):
            continue
        path, sep, rest = re.match(r"([^?#]*)([?#]?)(.*)", url).groups()
        if not path:
            continue
        target = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(f), path))
        links.setdefault(f, []).append((url, target, sep + rest))

# 2. move
moves = [(o, n) for o, n in MAPPING.items() if (ROOT / o).exists()]
for old, new in moves:
    print(f"git mv {old} {new}")
    if not DRY:
        (ROOT / new).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        git("mv", old, new)
if DRY:
    sys.exit(0)

# 3. rewrite markdown links from their new location
changed = 0
for old_md, items in links.items():
    new_md = remap(old_md)
    p = ROOT / new_md
    s = p.read_text()
    o = s
    for url, target, suffix in items:
        new_target = remap(target)
        if new_target == target and new_md == old_md:
            continue
        rel = os.path.relpath(new_target, os.path.dirname(new_md))
        if url.endswith("/") and not rel.endswith("/"):
            rel += "/"
        s = s.replace(f"]({url}", f"]({rel}{suffix}", 1) if f"]({url}" in s else s.replace(f"](<{url}", f"](<{rel}{suffix}", 1)
    if s != o:
        p.write_text(s)
        changed += 1
print(f"rewrote links in {changed} markdown files")

# 4. repo-root path strings: preceded by start, quote, whitespace, (, =, `, [ — never by '/' or '.'
now = [f for f in git("ls-files").split("\n") if f and f.endswith(TEXT) and not f.endswith(SKIP) and (ROOT / f).is_file()]
pat = re.compile(r"(?<![\w./-])(" + "|".join(re.escape(o) for o in sorted(MAPPING, key=len, reverse=True)) + r")(?=[/'\"`\s)\]:,]|$)")
n = 0
for f in now:
    p = ROOT / f
    s = p.read_text(errors="ignore")
    t = pat.sub(lambda m: MAPPING[m.group(1)], s)
    if t != s:
        p.write_text(t)
        n += 1
        print(f"  paths: {f}")
print(f"rewrote repo-root paths in {n} files")

# 101 Meydenbauer, Building B — under-slab waste re-pipe bid model

KEAD project 25-048. Bid due **October 30, 2026, 5:00 PM** (Invitation to Bid 00 11 16 §1.3).

This model converts the bid set's foundation-level waste plan into measured quantities and a 3D
view of the slab cuts, trenches and pipe. Its purpose is the bid. It tests the **700 SF slab
allowance** (Bid Form Allowance No. 7, Addendum 1), measures pipe by size, and sizes the
excavation that will be hauled through occupied units. It is an estimating and coordination aid,
not a contract document.

Results, renders and draft RFIs: [projects/meydenbauer-b/deliverables/underslab](../../deliverables/underslab/README.md).

## Pipeline

```bash
uv sync --group pdf
# sources/ is git-ignored; put the bid set there first
uv run python projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/prepare.py sources/meydenbauer/exhibit-a-bid-set.pdf
uv run python projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/takeoff.py          # takeoff.json + workbook
uv run python projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/build.py            # .blend, .glb, 8 renders (~11 min, 4 cores)
uv run python projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/build.py --no-render   # model + checks only (~3 s)
```

| Step | Reads | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prepare.py` | Exhibit A, page 6 (P1.02) | `meydenbauer-b.spec.json`, `build/meydenbauer-b/underlay_P1.02.png` |
| `takeoff.py` | spec | `build/meydenbauer-b/takeoff.json`, `Meydenbauer-B-underslab-takeoff.xlsx` |
| `build.py` | spec + takeoff | `.blend` (underlay packed), `.glb` (element properties as extras), `present-*.png`, `review-*.png`, `model-checks.json` |

4D films (construction-phase model in [REALISM.md](REALISM.md); results in
[projects/meydenbauer-b/deliverables/underslab/anim](../../deliverables/underslab/anim/README.md)):

```bash
uv run python projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/schedule.py         # strawman unit-by-unit schedule (rates assumed)
uv run python projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/logistics.py        # entries, staging, haul routes (assumed, SOR Fig 8)
uv run python projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/animate.py --plan sequence --fps 30 --no-render   # .blend + 92 + 44 checks
uv run python projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/animate.py --plan sequence --fps 30 --stills --res 0.4 --samples 12
PLAN=sequence bash projects/meydenbauer-b/products/underslab/runpod_animate.sh setup   # then bench, render 2, finish
```

| Step | Reads | Writes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schedule.py` | takeoff | `meydenbauer-b.schedule.json` (days per unit and phase, haul quantities) |
| `logistics.py` | shell, takeoff, schedule | `meydenbauer-b.logistics.json` (entries, site massing, routes, bins) |

Every construction project is now a **site**: `projects/<site>/` with `project.yaml`, `specs/` (spec-driven models), `products/<name>/` (bespoke pipelines with `product.yaml` steps run by `bm run`) and `deliverables/<name>/`.

| `field-parapet` | existing / proposed detail specs |
| `room-living-kitchen` | photo-only room spec |
| `sample` | CI pipeline fixture |
| `meydenbauer-b` | product `underslab` (bid model, realism, 4D) + its deliverables |
| `highland` | products `water`, `repipe`, `exterior`, `installation`, `walkthrough`; 8 deliverables |

## Commits
1. **`bm audit-blends`** opens every committed `.blend` (LFS included in CI) and fails on missing external files. The baseline run on this PR, before any move: **12 audited, 0 failed, every scene self-contained**, so the moves cannot break a scene's textures or links.
2. **Spec-only jobs → sites.** `specs/` and `takeoff/` are gone, and builds land in `build/<site>/<spec>/`. Also removes the cinema deliverable README (its film, stills and checks were never committed; agreed with the owner) and the stale `INSTRUCTIONS.md`.
3. **Meydenbauer → site.**
   - Its scripts imported Highland's `cinema_assets.py` via `sys.path`. That code is now the shared `bmodels.polyhaven`, and each project keeps only its own lists and lock file.
   - The CC0 HDRI moves to `assets/hdri/`.
   - New `bm check-products` runs each product's `check` step, and `build-models` runs it for changed products.
   - Note: the cinema scene signature now also hashes `polyhaven.py`, so a prepared cinema scene rebuilds once.
4. **Highland → site.**

PR 3 ([#26](https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models/pull/26)) is pushed and marked ready. CI is running in the background. Every jobsite now lives under `projects/<site>/`:

| Site | Contents |
|---|---|
| `qp-cottage-a`, `field-parapet`, `room-living-kitchen`, `sample` | specs (and takeoff) |
| `meydenbauer-b` | product `underslab` + deliverables |
| `highland` | products `water`, `repipe`, `exterior`, `installation`, `walkthrough` + 8 deliverables |

**Checked before and during the move:**
- **Scene files:** I added `bm audit-blends` and ran it in CI before anything moved. All 12 committed `.blend` files have every texture and asset packed inside, so moving folders can't break them.
- **Generated files:** after the move, the Highland `repipe` and `walkthrough` setup scripts regenerate their committed JSON byte for byte. Meydenbauer's bpy-free steps (takeoff → schedule → logistics) also run from the new paths.
- **Links:** every markdown link in the repo resolves.

**Changes beyond the plan:**
- **`highland-drone` stayed one product** (`walkthrough`) instead of the four I planned. Its scripts import each other and share one flight spec, so splitting them would only add links between products.
- **Code shared between sites.** Meydenbauer was loading Highland's asset code through a path hack. That code is now `bmodels.polyhaven`, used by both sites, and the shared sky image (HDRI) moved to `assets/hdri/`. One side effect: an already-prepared cinema scene will rebuild once on its next run.
- **Product checks in CI:** a new `bm check-products` runs each product's `check` step for any product that changed.
- **Duplicate removed:** 14 MB of identical copies in the archviz gallery (MP4, GIF, poster) are now links to the blender-film originals.
- **Removed, as you decided:** the cinema deliverable README. I also deleted the outdated `INSTRUCTIONS.md`.

**Not tested:** the GPU/RunPod renders and the Node/Playwright film builds. Their paths were updated by script and syntax-checked, but nothing actually ran.

**Small blemish:** one commit message lost the word "`check`" to shell quoting. Fixing it needed a force-push, which was blocked, and it isn't worth one.

**Your merge queue:** #24 → #25 → #26, each waiting on your approval in Entire Gates. All repo checks have passed so far on #24 and #25.

**Up next:**
- **PR 4:** large files go to Releases, with a pre-commit size guard.
- **PR 5:** `CLAUDE.md`, a slimmer README and `docs/`.
- **PR 6:** the remaining CI work. Most of it already landed in PRs 1–3.

Highland cinematic film: [shot list and rebuild](projects/highland/products/walkthrough/CINEMA.md) (the rendered film is not published in this repo).

## Pipeline (always in this order)

1. **Intake.** Inventory every source: sheet number, detail number, revision/date, scale, photo IDs. Read drawings at full resolution (rasterize PDFs with `pdftoppm -r 200+`; crop into details). Note scale bars and "NTS" details.
2. **Takeoff.** Extract every dimension, member size, spacing, elevation, and count into the model spec. Use actual lumber sizes (2x10 = 1½ × 9¼), not nominal. Never scale an NTS detail. Never infer a dimension from a partial drawing and call it documented.
3. **Model spec** (`projects/<site>/specs/<area>.yaml`; start a site with `uv run bm new <site>`). The spec is the single source of truth; geometry is never hand-edited in Blender without the spec changing too. Every element carries:
   - `status: confirmed` — dimension shown on a document (`source` required)
   - `status: provisional` — derived: scaled from a drawing with a scale bar, or measured from a photo against a known reference (`source` required; note the reference and expected tolerance)
   - `status: assumed` — not in any document (`basis` required, e.g. "code-minimum", "typical", "massing only")
   - Document-driven `checks`: counts, overall extents, clear gaps, spacing, elevations — each with its `source`.
4. **Build.** `uv run bm build <site>[/<spec>] [--realistic]` (bpy, headless). One collection per trade; trades stay separate. Inches in the spec; Blender stores meters, displays imperial.
5. **Verify.** The builder fails (exit 1) on: missing source/basis, count or extent mismatch, gap mismatch, or a blank render. Then look at the review renders myself — plan, front, side, iso — colored by provenance (green confirmed, yellow provisional, orange assumed). Where a drawing elevation exists, compare the ortho render against it at the same scale. "Checks passed" and "looked right" are both required; report which were done.
6. **Realism pass** (only after geometry is verified). PBR materials by real product where known; realistic lighting via Cycles. Realism never changes geometry.
7. **Quantities.** Every house build writes `<name>_takeoff.xlsx` (src/bmodels/qto.py): openings schedule, siding + gable panel net of openings by elevation, casing and corner-board LF, roof area by pitch, squares (waste is a yellow input), ridge/hip/valley/eave/rake LF, and an Elements sheet of stable IDs for trackers. - **Every extracted opening must appear on an elevation** or it is rejected (tubs, showers, garage-door lines and revision clouds all produce false openings). Record rejected candidates in the spec.
- **Revision clouds and tags break linework** — look for missing wall where a cloud crosses, trace it manually, and add it as an `extra_walls` entry with its reason.
- **Mirror-image units:** extract the cleaner half and mirror, but first measure the match (Cottage A: 94% of walls within 1½").
- **Roofs:** union of convex hip/gable pieces taken from the eave outline on the roof plan; verify predicted ridge/hip positions against the drawn ones and ridge heights against elevations.
- **Walls are built boolean-free** (rectangle decomposition, openings cut by box splitting). Roof unions use Blender's **Manifold** boolean solver — the Exact solver fails on the coplanar faces that roofs inevitably have.
- **Overlay check:** `src/bmodels/overlay.py` renders the model orthographically at the drawing's scale and overlays it on the elevation; report the edge-agreement % and look at the image.

# Blender models of construction projects

Dimensionally accurate, provenance-tracked 3D models of restoration and defect-repair work in occupied
multifamily buildings, built headless in Blender from construction drawings, details, specs and site photos.
Accuracy first, realism second: every dimension traces to a source or is labeled assumed, automated checks
must pass, and the renders get looked at. How models are made: **[docs/METHOD.md](docs/METHOD.md)** ·
step-by-step commands: **[docs/RUNBOOK.md](docs/RUNBOOK.md)**.

## Quickstart

```bash
uv sync                                   # Python 3.11 + locked bpy 5.0.1, PyMuPDF, OpenCV (one environment)
uvx pre-commit install                    # once per clone: blocks oversized or unsourced commits
uv run bm list                            # sites, specs, products
uv run bm new <site> --type detail        # start a project from templates/project/
uv run bm build <site>                    # build + verify every spec of a site (or <site>/<spec>)
uv run bm check                           # provenance, metadata, large files, links, tests
```

Linux needs the X11 libraries bpy links against:
`sudo apt-get install libx11-6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxi6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libice6 libgl1`.
Always run Python through uv (`uv run python …`, `uv run bm …`). Node pieces (browser viewers, Playwright
films) use npm inside their product folder.

## Layout

```
projects/<site>/
  project.yaml               name, address, building type, scope, release tag prefix
  sources/manifest.json      inventory of drawings and photos (the files themselves stay out of git)
  specs/*.yaml               spec-driven models: detail | house | room | element  → `bm build`
  takeoff/                   extracted plan data the specs read
  products/<name>/           bespoke pipelines (films, viewers, bid models) + product.yaml steps → `bm run`
  deliverables/<name>/       what gets handed over: READMEs, previews; large files via Releases
src/bmodels/                 the shared toolkit and the `bm` CLI
templates/project/           what `bm new` copies
assets/                      shared CC0 assets (HDRIs)
render/                      saved-scene shot catalog for the render-scenes workflow
docs/                        METHOD.md, RUNBOOK.md
```

## Sites

| Site | Name | Specs | Products |
|---|---|---|---|
| [field-parapet](projects/field-parapet/) | Field parapet (site photo P1) | field-parapet-existing, field-parapet-proposed | — |
| [highland](projects/highland/) | 200 W. Highland condominiums | — | exterior, installation, repipe, walkthrough, water |
| [meydenbauer-b](projects/meydenbauer-b/) | 101 Meydenbauer, Building B | — | underslab |
| [qp-cottage-a](projects/qp-cottage-a/) | Quail Park of Lynnwood — Cottage Duplex A | qp-cottage-a, qp-rake-ah700-12 | — |

Regenerate with `uv run bm list --markdown`. Highlights: Highland
[archviz walkthrough](projects/highland/deliverables/archviz/README.md),
[installation film](projects/highland/deliverables/installation/README.md),
[cinema shot list](projects/highland/products/walkthrough/CINEMA.md) (film not published);
Meydenbauer [bid model, realism views and 4D films](projects/meydenbauer-b/deliverables/underslab/README.md).

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `bm build [path \| site \| site/spec] [--realistic] [--changed BASE]` | build, verify and render specs → `build/<site>/<spec>/` |
| `bm run <site>/<product> <step> [args]` | run a step declared in `product.yaml` |
| `bm check [--staged \| --base REF]` · `bm check-products` | repo checks · every product's `check` step |
| `bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>` · `bm assets pull\|verify <manifest>` | large outputs to/from GitHub Releases |

| Workflow | When | What |
|---|---|---|
| `build-models` | specs, takeoff, products, `src/`, lock change | `bm build --changed` (every spec when code or the lock changes) and `bm check-products`; reports in the job summary, `build/` as artifact |
| `checks` | every PR and push to main | `bm check --base …` (provenance, metadata, large files, links, tests) and `bm audit-blends` |

`uv.lock`, `uv sync --frozen`). Pushes from a local clone can change workflow files; cloud agent tokens
without the `workflow` scope cannot.

## Working style

Ask once, batched, only for what the documents can't answer (a missing detail, which revision governs).

- **`.claude/settings.json`**: Claude Code hooks that call `entire hooks claude-code …` on session and subagent events. Each command does nothing on a machine without `entire`.

Both are shared project config that's meant to be committed, so everyone who clones the repo gets the same Entire setup. You're currently on `workflow/ci-lock` (PR #29).
